title: Monic relations give a finite monogenic residue-field extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $B$ a commutative $k$-algebra, and $\mathfrak q\subset B[T]$ a prime ideal containing a monic polynomial $f=T^d+\sum_{j<d}c_jT^j$ with $d>0$, where monic means leading coefficient $1$. Set $\mathfrak p=\{b\in B:b\in\mathfrak q\}$ under the constant-polynomial inclusion, $F=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $E=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Using the canonical identifications $F\cong\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak p)$ and $E\cong\operatorname{Frac}(B[T]/\mathfrak q)$, the injective map $B/\mathfrak p\to B[T]/\mathfrak q$ extends to a $k$-embedding $F\hookrightarrow E$ sending $\bar b/\bar c$ to the quotient of their images. If $\xi\in E$ is the image of $T$, then $$E=F[\xi],\qquad E=\operatorname{span}_F\{1,\xi,\ldots,\xi^{d-1}\}.$$ Here $F[\xi]$ is the subring of polynomials in $\xi$ with coefficients in $F$; the second equality means every element of $E$ is an $F$-linear combination of those powers. Thus $E/F$ is finite-dimensional [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], every element of $E$ is algebraic over $F$ (satisfies a nonzero polynomial over $F$), and $$\operatorname{trdeg}_k E=\operatorname{trdeg}_k F$$ as cardinal transcendence degrees [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. No domain, Noetherian, or finite-type hypothesis on $B$ is imposed.

proof.text: Put $A=B/\mathfrak p$ and $D=B[T]/\mathfrak q$. The contraction $\mathfrak p$ is prime: $bc\in\mathfrak p$ implies $bc\in\mathfrak q$, hence $b$ or $c$ lies in $\mathfrak p$, and $1\notin\mathfrak p$. The map $A\to D$ is injective because its kernel consists exactly of constants in $\mathfrak q$. The residue-field lemma identifies $F=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ and $E=\operatorname{Frac}(D)$. Apply the fraction-field lift to $A\hookrightarrow D\hookrightarrow E$. It gives an embedding $F\hookrightarrow E$ with $\bar b/\bar c\mapsto\bar b\,\bar c^{-1}$. On $k$ this agrees with the given coefficient map, so it is a $k$-embedding.

source.place: Tag 051P (lemma-refined-Noether-normalization), residue-field inclusion; local-rings paragraph identifying residue fields with fraction fields after Tag 07BI, using Tag 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient).

proof.text: Map the coefficients of $f$ along $B\to A\to F$, obtaining $g=T^d+\sum_{j<d}\bar c_jT^j\in F[T]$. Its leading coefficient is still $1$, so its degree is $d$. With $\xi$ the image of $T$ in $E$, evaluation gives $g(\xi)=0$ since $f\in\mathfrak q$. Let $S=F[\xi]\subseteq E$. Evaluation therefore induces a surjective $F$-linear map $F[T]/(g)\to S$: it sends the class of $\sum a_jT^j$ to $\sum a_j\xi^j$, and multiples of $g$ evaluate to zero. The monic-quotient lemma gives a basis $1,T,\ldots,T^{d-1}$ in the source. Taking images shows $S=\operatorname{span}_F\{1,\xi,\ldots,\xi^{d-1}\}$; by the definition of finite generation this is a finite-dimensional $F$-algebra.

source.place: Tag 051P (lemma-refined-Noether-normalization), finite residue extension from the monic relation; Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), proof of 10=>1, the finite free monic quotient.

proof.text: The subring $S\subseteq E$ is a commutative domain: $1\ne0$, and a product vanishes only if one factor does, since this holds in $E$. Apply the finite-dimensional-domain lemma over the field $F$ to conclude that every nonzero element of $S$ has an inverse in $S$. The image of $D$ is contained in $S$, because a class of $\sum b_jT^j$ maps to $\sum\bar b_j\xi^j$. By the residue-field lemma every $e\in E$ is $u/v$ with $u,v\in D$ and $v\ne0$. Their images belong to $S$, the image of $v$ is nonzero by injectivity, and its inverse in $S$ equals its inverse in $E$. Thus $e\in S$. Consequently $E=S$, giving both asserted equalities and finite dimensionality.

source.place: Tag 051P (lemma-refined-Noether-normalization), finite residue-extension assertion, expanded using the finite-dimensional-domain field criterion and the residue fraction-field description.

proof.text: Apply the finite-algebra integrality lemma to $F\to E$, which is module-finite by steps 2 and 3. Every $e\in E$ satisfies a monic polynomial in $F[T]$. That polynomial is nonzero because its leading coefficient is $1\ne0$ in the field $F$. Thus every element of $E$ is algebraic over $F$.

The maps $k\to F\to E$ form a compatible tower by step 1. The transcendence-degree tower lemma, including its algebraicity criterion, gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_F E=0$ by step 4 and $\operatorname{trdeg}_k E=\operatorname{trdeg}_k F+\operatorname{trdeg}_F E=\operatorname{trdeg}_k F$. These are cardinal equalities; no finiteness of either transcendence degree is used.
